# Public plugin API readiness

<!-- Generated by wasm/scripts/sync-reference-docs.cjs. Edit the source catalog, not this file. -->

> **Decision:** Deferred for general compiler hooks and isolated untrusted plugins. Trusted external lowerers are available.

Pulse 1.0.0-beta.10 supports versioned trusted package lowerers independently of npm package versions. Provider bootstrap is explicit and exact. The current boundaries are:

- **Lowerers:** trusted first-party and third-party build dependencies admitted by versioned contracts; import-resolved package ownership; no package allowlist or compiler-release version equality; no sandbox.
- **Providers:** explicit package selection through pulse.provider-toolchain.v1; bare host IDs use the @pulse-compute/provider-<id> convention, scoped names are exact, and none is internal; no scanning or self-registration.

## Readiness requirements

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| `trustModel` | **Not implemented** |
| `packageDiscovery` | **Not implemented** |
| `versionNegotiation` | **Not implemented** |
| `securityPolicy` | **Not implemented** |
| `compatibilityContract` | **Not implemented** |
| `isolatedPackageLoading` | **Not implemented** |

The trusted package-lowerer contract and explicit provider toolchain are available scoped extension seams. This readiness record concerns general compiler hooks and isolated untrusted plugins; it does not gate trusted external lowerers.

The machine-readable readiness record and release validation enforce this
boundary. See the [trusted package-lowerer contract](../contributing/package-lowerer-contract.md)
and [provider toolchain](../contributing/adding-core-provider.md). Lowerers run
ordinary Node code without a sandbox; providers use explicit selection.

Machine-readable status is published as [`plugin-readiness.json`](./plugin-readiness.json).
